findings.recommendation: Remove `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` so `order_id`, `customer_id` and `total_cents` keep their snake_case names and only `currency` is added. Today `GET /orders/{id}` serializes `orderId`, `customerId` and `totalCents`, so every partner integration reading `order_id`, `customer_id` or `total_cents` gets a missing field on the first response after deployment, with no warning. This breaks the documented contract in docs/api.md ("a field is never renamed or removed without two releases of deprecation"), is not marked **BREAKING**, and is absent from the release note, which only announces the added `currency`. If camelCase is ever wanted, emit both names during two releases of deprecation and announce it as BREAKING.
findings.title: `rename_all = "camelCase"` renames every existing order JSON field

findings.evidence:
/// The currency of orders that do not name one (ISO 4217).
pub default_currency: String,
findings.recommendation: Give the new key a default that matches today's behavior, e.g. `#[serde(default = "default_currency")]` returning `"EUR"`, and add a test loading a config without the key. As written, `Config` derives `Deserialize` with a required `default_currency`, so every deployed `config.toml` written before this change (only `database_url` and `listen`) makes `config::load` fail with "missing field `default_currency`" and the service does not start after the upgrade. Only config.example.toml was updated; no migration step or release-note item tells operators to add the key.
findings.title: Existing `config.toml` files without `default_currency` no longer load
